skill.name: geniml
skill.description: Plan and run Geniml workflows for BED-based genomic machine learning. Covers Region2Vec, BEDspace, scEmbed, consensus peak universes, and utility tools.

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, example code, legitimate cache paths, or scientific terminology. One low-risk supply-chain issue remains: the skill documents an unpinned GitHub development install that can fetch remote code if used. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer PyPI releases, or pin the GitHub install to a commit or signed release. Label development installs as optional.
Explain what is stored in ~/.bedcache and show how to choose an explicit project cache directory.

remediation.issue: Executable examples are mixed with narrative
remediation.suggestion: Mark shell commands as manual examples and avoid implying that the skill should install software automatically.

content.value_statement: Genomic interval projects need consistent preprocessing, embedding training, and universe construction. This skill guides Geniml workflows for BED files, scATAC-seq data, and model evaluation.
actual_capabilities: Install Geniml from PyPI and choose optional machine learning dependencies.
Train Region2Vec embeddings from tokenized BED file collections.
Build BEDspace models for joint region and metadata search.
Run scEmbed workflows for single-cell ATAC-seq embeddings and scanpy integration.
Create and evaluate consensus peak universes with CC, CCF, ML, or HMM methods.
Use BBClient, BEDshift, tokenization, evaluation, and search utilities.
limitations: It does not validate biological assumptions or genome assembly choices.
Large datasets may require substantial memory, storage, and compute resources.
Some workflows depend on external tools, including StarSpace and uniwig.
Reference commands are examples and may need version-specific adjustment.

use_cases.title: Train Region Embeddings
use_cases.description: Prepare BED files, tokenize against a universe, and train Region2Vec features for downstream analysis.

use_cases.title: Analyze Single-Cell Accessibility
use_cases.description: Use scEmbed guidance to create cell embeddings, cluster cells, and integrate results with scanpy.

use_cases.title: Build Searchable Genomic Collections
use_cases.description: Combine BEDspace embeddings with metadata to support similarity search across regions and labels.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Geniml Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: I have BED files and metadata. Help me choose a Geniml workflow and list the required inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Consensus Universe
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through building a consensus peak universe from multiple BED files using Geniml. Include parameter choices and quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Train Region2Vec Embeddings
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Region2Vec workflow for these BED files and this universe. Include tokenization, training parameters, and evaluation metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Design a BEDspace Search Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an advanced BEDspace pipeline for metadata-aware genomic search. Include preprocessing, training, distance calculation, and validation.

output_examples.input: A user wants metadata-aware search over BED file collections.
output: Recommended BEDspace for joint region and label embeddings.

best_practices: Confirm genome assembly, chromosome sizes, and universe choice before tokenization.
Record parameters, random seeds, software versions, and input file provenance.
Evaluate embeddings with multiple metrics and visual review before interpretation.
anti_patterns: Do not mix BED files from different genome assemblies without liftover.
Do not train embeddings before checking tokenization coverage.
Do not use development installs in production without pinning a revision.

faq.question: What data does this skill work with?
faq.answer: It works with genomic interval data, especially BED files and scATAC-seq datasets.

faq.question: Can it build consensus peak universes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains CC, CCF, ML, and HMM methods for building universe files.

faq.question: Does it support single-cell ATAC-seq workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers scEmbed workflows and integration with scanpy objects.

faq.question: Does it run Geniml automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and example commands that users should review before running.

faq.question: What external dependencies may be needed?
faq.answer: Some workflows may need PyTorch, uniwig, StarSpace, scanpy, or reticulate.

faq.question: Is this suitable for production genomics pipelines?
faq.answer: Use it as workflow guidance. Pin package versions, validate inputs, and review commands before production use.
